title: Listening Section 3 - Student Project Discussion
instruction: You will hear two students, Priya and Marcus, discussing a project about food waste in their university canteen. Answer Questions 1-10.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: Marcus, have you had a chance to read the brief for our environmental science project?

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Yes. I think we should look at food waste in the canteen, rather than the recycling topic.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: I agree. Though Ms Cole said we need a clear focus. Should we study all food, or just one type?

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Just one. When I volunteered in the kitchen last term, the staff told me that more bread was thrown away than anything else, so I'd say bread.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: Good idea. How should we collect the data?

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: We could weigh the bin each evening, and also survey students about their habits. I was thinking of fifty students.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: Fifty is too few to give reliable results. Let's ask eighty.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: All right, eighty it is. When shall we start weighing?

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: Exams begin on the fifteenth, and the canteen is quieter during exams, so we shouldn't start then. Why not the week beginning the eighth of May?

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: That's fine. Do you think the kitchen manager will agree?

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: I spoke to him yesterday. He's happy as long as we wear gloves when we handle the waste.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Good. Afterwards we'll need to enter the figures into a spreadsheet. Shall I do the analysis?

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: I did the statistics module last year, so I'll take that on. You could write the introduction instead.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Fine. How long does the report have to be?

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: Two thousand words. I thought the deadline was the fourth of June.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: No, I checked the student portal this morning. It's the fourteenth.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: That's better, we'll have more time. What about the recommendations at the end?

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: We could suggest smaller portions.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: That would be hard to enforce, since students choose their own. What about selling the unused bread cheaply at the end of the day? It would be popular with students.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: That's a good idea. Let's recommend that.

transcript.speaker: Priya
transcript.text: Great. I'll write up what we've agreed and send it to you tonight.

questions.explanation: Priya says fifty is too few to give reliable results.

options.optionText: A. It would be too expensive.
B. It would give unreliable results.
C. It would take too long.

questions.explanation: He is happy as long as they wear gloves.

options.optionText: B. Weighing must take place after closing time.
C. A tutor must be present.
